title: U.S. House · Illinois's 7th District
area: Chicago's West Side and near-west suburbs, including Austin, Oak Park, and a corridor extending northwest toward Elgin and Streamwood.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Danny K. Davis did not run for re-election. La Shawn Ford won a crowded March 17, 2026 Democratic primary with 23.7% of the vote over Melissa Conyears-Ervin (20.5%), Anthony Driver Jr. (11.6%), Kina Collins (9.5%) and nine other candidates. Chad Koppie ran unopposed for the Republican nomination. Lien Choi, an independent candidate, also qualified for the November ballot. Ballotpedia calculated the district's Cook Partisan Voter Index as D+34, based on the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections.

summary.text: Ford is the Democratic nominee for the open Illinois 7th District seat. A former Chicago public school teacher and real estate entrepreneur, he has served in the Illinois House of Representatives for the West Side's 8th District since 2007 and ran for Chicago mayor in 2019. He won the March 2026 Democratic primary in a crowded field with about 24% of the vote.

background.text: According to his state legislative website, he is a lifelong Chicago resident who was raised by a single mother.
Received a bachelor's degree in education from Loyola University, Chicago.

Worked as a teacher in the Chicago public school system and founded a real estate business; his campaign website says he bought and sold his first building in college and started the business while still teaching.
Was elected to the Illinois House of Representatives for the 8th District in 2007 and has been re-elected since; he is not seeking re-election to that seat in 2026.

Has chaired the Appropriations-Higher Education Committee in recent sessions. His campaign website says he created and chaired the House Small Business Empowerment and Workforce Development Committee and sponsored the State Employment Application Act ("Ban the Box") and a law making Juneteenth a state holiday.
Established the Council on Responsible Fatherhood, according to his state legislative website.
Was a candidate in the February 2019 nonpartisan Chicago mayoral election.

In November 2012 was indicted by a federal grand jury on 17 counts of bank fraud and providing false information to a bank; in August 2014 he pleaded guilty to one misdemeanor tax count in exchange for the 17 felony charges being dropped, and in November 2014 was sentenced to six months' probation and 100 hours of community service.

Ballotpedia lists board and organization memberships including the Austin YMCA board, Austin Chamber of Commerce board and Circle Family Care, and says he has one child; his campaign website lists service on the Boy Scouts Pathway to Adventure Council board.

priorities.text: On public health, says he would preserve and expand access to Medicaid and SNAP benefits, citing legislation he says he passed that increased healthcare coverage and improved school nutrition.
Says he would work to lower the cost of living by making housing, education and child care more affordable, pointing to legislation he sponsored that funded education and supported housing stability.
On the economy, says he would work to create jobs and support small businesses, citing his experience as a real estate business owner.
priorities.quote: I know how vital small businesses are to the vibrancy of our communities.

positions.summary: Says he would preserve and expand access to Medicaid and SNAP benefits.

record.text: Has chaired the Illinois House Appropriations-Higher Education Committee in the 2019-2020, 2021-2022, 2023-2024 and 2025-2026 sessions.

Pleaded guilty in federal court in August 2014 to one misdemeanor count of filing a false tax return, after being indicted in 2012 on eight counts of bank fraud and nine counts of providing false information to a bank; the felony charges were dropped and he was sentenced to six months' probation and 100 hours of community service.

summary.text: Koppie is the Republican nominee for Illinois' 7th District. A former Delta Air Lines jet captain and farmer, he has served on local school boards and as a township trustee and has run for office repeatedly, including as the 2022 and 2024 general-election candidate in this district. He won the March 2026 Republican primary over Patricia Easley, 65% to 35%.

background.text: Attended aviation school at Purdue University.
Worked as a jet captain with Delta Airlines and as a farmer; Ballotpedia lists his profession as farmer.
Served as a member of the Kane County Regional Board of Schools, a board member of the Illinois Forum, a township trustee, and a local school board member.
Was chosen at the Constitution Party's March 2018 nominating convention as its lieutenant gubernatorial nominee, and appears on Ballotpedia as a Constitution Party candidate for U.S. Senate in 2020.
Ran in the 2022 Republican primary for Illinois' 8th District, which Chris Dargis won, and was a candidate in the 2022 general election in the 7th District, which Rep. Danny K. Davis won.
Was the unopposed Republican primary winner in March 2024 and received 16.7% of the vote against Davis in the November 2024 general election.
Won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary over Patricia Easley and is on the November 3, 2026 ballot for the open seat.

priorities.text: Says he would vote for legislation protecting human life from conception, describing abortion as a departure from the nation's founding values.
Wants Congress to cut spending from each federal department and agency by at least 3% annually, cut tax rates accordingly, and abolish the Federal Reserve.
Supports building a wall along the U.S.-Mexico border and says ICE should arrest and deport all people in the country illegally.
priorities.quote: Chad supports building the wall, along the Mexican border. He says that ICE should try to arrest and deport all illegal aliens.

positions.summary: Says he would vote in Congress for protection of human life in the womb, opposing abortion.
Supports the Second Amendment and says he would never vote for gun-control legislation.
positions.quote: Chad supports the 2nd Amendment. He knows that law-abiding Americans can own guns to defend themselves. He'll never vote for any gun control bills.

positions.summary: Supports building a border wall and says ICE should arrest and deport people in the country illegally.
positions.quote: Chad supports building the wall, along the Mexican border. He says that ICE should try to arrest and deport all illegal aliens.

candidates.name: Lien Choi
candidates.ballotNote: Qualified as an independent write-in candidate for the November general election.

summary.text: Choi is an independent write-in candidate in Illinois' 7th District. According to Ballotpedia, Choi holds a bachelor's degree from the Illinois Institute of Technology and has worked in construction and as a director at a homeless shelter. In a Ballotpedia survey, Choi calls themself progressive and lists campaign finance reform as the main campaign message.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from the Illinois Institute of Technology in 2012.
Career experience includes working in construction and as a director at Hope House Homeless Shelter and Transitional Housing, according to Ballotpedia.
In a 2026 Ballotpedia survey, describes themself as independent, progressive, egalitarian, a "compassionate secular humanist," disabled and poor, and says they have experienced homelessness.
Wrote in the survey: "I have seen both sides of how life should be and the struggle that can devastate lives."
background.quote: I am one who needs the help that every American deserves and I desperately want a country that every American deserves.

background.text: Was also a write-in candidate for this seat in the 2024 general election.

priorities.text: Supports campaign finance reform, saying the political system's problems come from the type of people elected rather than the structure itself.
Supports universal healthcare and a universal basic income.

researchNotes: Koppie has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his positions are drawn from his campaign website as quoted on Ballotpedia. Lien Choi completed a 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website was found, and the survey and Ballotpedia profile do not state pronouns or birthplace. Koppie won the 2026 Republican primary over Patricia Easley (65% to 35%); he was not unopposed.
